subject: 🏃 Thursday — 6 mi Progression Run (Wk 7, Presidio Pivot Week)
html:
Tomorrow: 6-mile progression run — the last running touch before Sunday's Presidio Half Marathon pivot test. This is a taper sharpener: wake the legs up with a short MP close, then shut it down. Not a fitness session.

Pre-run activation (5 min): Quadruped hip CARs (3 each direction) → banded lateral walks (10 each) → glute bridges (10 reps, 2-sec hold) → PT-prescribed quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 reps each side).

The run:

  • First 4 miles — easy, HR ≤145 (Z2, conversational). Door route, pace floats with the hills. No target pace — just keep the HR honest.
  • Last 2 miles — marathon pace, HR 150–160. Pace readout ~7:35–7:45 on flat, slower on climbs. If you find a relatively flat stretch for these, great, but HR governs — don't chase the pace number. Cap at 160; if HR wants to drift higher, let the pace soften.

Focus cue: Smooth and controlled on the MP close. You're sharpening three days out from a gated half marathon, not building fitness. The MP miles should feel like comfortable cruising at effort — if you're digging, back off. Bank the freshness for Sunday.

Where you are: Week 7 of 12, Phase 2. Presidio HM pivot test is Sunday (June 21) — 3 days out. The three gates: sub-1:37:30 finish, avg HR <170 final 3 mi, zero knee compensation. Tuesday's track sharpener was textbook (3×1600m at 7:09–7:13/mi, HR 155–158, dead-even splits). Yesterday's heavy strength was time-cut (3×6 squat/RDL, calf dropped) but knee 1/5 throughout — less accumulated fatigue than a full session, so legs may feel unusually fresh tomorrow. Don't interpret that as a green light to push harder; put it in the bank for Sunday.

Tonight: Lay out your run kit, set the alarm, bed by 10. Fri is the stability lift, Sat is full rest, then the gated test. The next 72 hours are about arriving at the start line fresh with a quiet knee — protect both.
